trial_title: Beneficial and Harmful Effects of Azathioprine and Allopurinol Versus Standard Azathioprine Therapy for Patients With Ulcerative Colitis
brief_summary:
Azathioprine is considered first line immunomodulatory therapy for patients with ulcerative colitis. Up to 50% are treatment failures or experience adverse events leading to treatment withdrawal. Recent evidence suggests that the combination of allopurinol and low dose azathioprine increases the proportion of treatment responders and reduce the risk of adverse events.

Objectives: To evaluate the beneficial and harmful effects of low dose azathioprine and allopurinol versus standard azathioprine

eligibility_table.justification: The patient is 22 years old and likely willing to comply with trial procedures.

eligibility_table.criterion: Clinically and histologically verified ulcerative colitis eligible for treatment with thiopurines due to steroid dependence (failure to taper steroid or starting a second course of systemic steroids within 1 year) or patients with the need for rescue therapy with anti-TumorNecrosisFactorα (anti-TNFα)
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has systemic mastocytosis, not ulcerative colitis, and does not meet the criteria for thiopurines or anti-TNFα.

eligibility_table.criterion: A sigmoidoscopy or colonoscopy showing active inflammation during the present disease flare
eligibility_table.justification: There is no indication of active inflammation in the colon or rectum as the patient has systemic mastocytosis.
